name: get_traffic_timeline
title: Traffic over time and onset of a problem
description: Dates a problem. Returns about thirty points of traffic over the window (requests, 4xx, 5xx, P95 response time) and the onset: the first interval that departs from the baseline. Use the onset time to look for what changed just before, with list_recent_changes.

environment.description: Id, HRID or name of an environment of your organization. Omit when `api` names an API that exists in only one environment you can read, or when you can read only one.

api.description: Id or exact name of an API. Use the id when several APIs share a name. Omit to look at the whole environment.

window.description: Length of the time range to look at, ending at `until`: a number followed by m, h or d, for example 15m, 2h or 1d. Default 15m. Never an epoch value.

until.description: End of the time range as an ISO-8601 UTC instant, for example 2026-01-31T14:00:00Z. Default: now. Set it to look at a past incident.

baselinePerInterval.description: What one interval looked like, on average, in the range of equal length before the window.

onset.description: Absent when no interval departs from the baseline.

at.description: Start of the first departing interval, ISO-8601 UTC.

responseTimeP95Ms.description: 95th percentile of the time to answer the consumer, backend included, in milliseconds. Absent without traffic.

endpointResponseTimeP95Ms.description: 95th percentile of the time spent waiting for the backend, in milliseconds. Close to responseTimeP95Ms when the backend is the slow part; far below it when the gateway is.

kind.description: SERVER_ERROR_RATE_UP: 5xx, the gateway or a backend fails. CLIENT_ERROR_RATE_UP: 4xx, requests are rejected (credentials, quota, input). LATENCY_UP: P95 response time. TRAFFIC_DROP: half the requests or fewer.
